**Finding submitted: `missing` (INSURANCE), confidence 0.9**

**What I checked**
- Full-document search for "insurance" — only hit is `p0012`, the net-revenue definition deducting "taxes, freight, insurance, refunds or credits," which is not a coverage obligation.
- Section outline — no insurance heading anywhere, including the exhibits.
- Both planner candidates read in full: § 14 Miscellaneous (14.1–14.10: assignment, waiver, law/arbitration, notices, independent contractors, severability, force majeure, subcontract, bankruptcy, entire agreement) and § 8 Indemnification (IP infringement only). Neither carries insurance.
- Searched "premises" (no hits) and read § 5 to confirm the vendor-side exposure.

**Direction check**
Commerce One is the counterparty/vendor: it provides an on-site operations consultant (5.1), professional services access for our first three implementations (5.2, 5.6), support and training (5.3, 5.5), and the MarketSite.net Service that handles Corio and Customer data. So the obligation properly binds them, not us.

**Classification**
No insurance clause exists at all for a vendor whose personnel support our hosted environment and whose service processes our and our Customers' data — that is the rule's walk-away scenario, not a near-fallback shortfall, so it is recorded as missing with an insert rather than noted in passing.

**Redline (validated ok:true)**
New § 14.10 at the preferred position — CGL USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate, E&O USD 2M, cyber/privacy USD 5M where Corio or Customer data is processed, statutory workers' compensation, term plus one year, certificates on request. To keep the insert clean I also renumbered the existing "14.10 Complete Understanding" to 14.11 rather than leaving a duplicate number. The comment offers the fallback (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M) in case the limits are resisted.
